subject: Post-call: trial handoff cheat sheet + ownership lanes
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@everlyhealth.com>, Tom Brown <tom.brown@everlyhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: trial handoff cheat sheet + ownership lanes

Hi Lydia / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a lightweight "cheat sheet" for the trial handoff so everyone's aligned before we kick off:

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use case: near-real-time clinical note summarization and search for care ops.
- Target scope for POC: ingest ~200k tokens / day from QA logs, evaluate latency and summary quality on 30k notes.
- Compliance: must support customer-managed KMS and meet our baseline SOC2 controls.

Proposed success criteria (initial)
1) Latency: 95th percentile < 500ms for single-note summarize (avg length ~600 tokens)
2) Quality: F1 on entity extraction > 0.82 vs your labeled set (sample: 2k notes)
3) Cost: token cost per 1k-notes <= estimate in shared sheet
4) Reliability: 99.5% availability during business hours (9am–6pm ET) during trial window

Ownership lanes (who-does-what) — please confirm if this matches your org:
- Infra (GPU / VPC / network): Redwood infra lead + Everly infra contact (we recommend Karthik Iyer as technical lead on our side)
- App / integration (ingest, connectors): Everly app team (Tom) for connector access; Marissa will handle SDK integration support
- Security & compliance (KMS, data retention, audit): Combined working group. Ben will take Redwood security lead; please confirm your security contact.
- Procurement / contracting: Lydia (Everly) + Camila (Redwood) for scope, invoicing windows, and any MSA addenda.

Operational decision routes (quick)
- If the trial requires additional keys (HSM/KMS), Security lead escalation -> sprints will pause until KMS access is confirmed (target resolution: 72 hours).
- If infra capacity exceeds baseline, Redwood will propose short-term burst credits for the trial; procurement to approve within 5 business days.

Next steps / proposed schedule
- Please confirm security contact and procurement timeline by EOD Friday (6/13).
- Internal kickoff: target Tues 6/24 for sandbox access + initial data push.
- Shared docs: initial cheat sheet + QA spreadsheet attached.

Attachments: 20250612-trial-cheat-sheet-v1.pdf, everly-qa-spreadsheet.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 15m if useful.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.inference

From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@everlyhealth.com>

Camila — thanks for the clear recap and the cheat sheet. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement: We're aiming to clear procurement approvals by 6/23 (we have a monthly vendor window). My procurement lead is copied: Tom, who will serve as point for integration access.
- Security: Our security lead is Lydia (me) for compliance intake; but I'll loop in our infra security engineer (Javier M.). We need to confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (yes/no) and whether the KV cache persists to disk. Can Ben confirm that?
- Acceptance criteria: the latency and quality metrics look reasonable; can we add a smoke test that verifies anonymization (test vector: 500 notes)?

We are prepared to proceed with a 30-day sandbox trial once we align on the security gating items.

Appreciate it — will follow up with Javier's contact and procurement docs.

Best,
Lydia Park
